paragraph: Single-family is the market here: 27 sales over six months at a median of $1,270,000, a sale-to-list ratio of 1.02, two-thirds of homes closing above asking, and a median of 12 days on market. That is a real seller's market, with many multiple offer situations. Sale prices ran from $210,000 up to $2.2 million, so the range is unusually wide and the median is the better guide to what you'll actually compete for. Condos and townhouses are a small, tight tier: 8 sales at a median of $1,295,000, every one of them between $901,000 and $1,335,000, with a 0.98 sale-to-list ratio and 22 days on market. Attached housing here is not the entry point. It prices right alongside the houses, and sellers in that tier are more willing to wait for the right buyer. On seasonality, monthly closings run between one and seven, too thin to call a trend from any single month. Across the six months the medians bounce without a clear direction. If you're weighing the two tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance lifestyle of a townhouse at a similar number.
